expected_level_description: You can: - turn complex data into compelling, clear and actionable stories - share data communication skills with the team and across government - present analysis and visualisations in clear ways to communicate complex messages - communicate negative and positive information to stakeholders - give tactical and strategic recommendations

skill: Communicating between the technical and non-technical
expected_level_description: You can: - listen to and interpret the needs of technical and non-technical stakeholders, and manage their expectations - manage active and reactive communication - support or host difficult discussions within the team or with diverse senior stakeholders

You can: - work with stakeholders to identify and address ethical and privacy concerns - demonstrate and communicate how data ethical issues fit into the wider organisational context - research developments in data ethics and privacy to improve compliance and processes - assess and constructively challenge proposed data ethics policies

You can: - implement and monitor data governance using standard methodology throughout the data life cycle, within a large organisation - meet the requirement for relevant data governance accreditation - take responsibility for specific parts of a data governance framework within the organisation

You can: - test and evaluate the feasibility of unfamiliar and emerging technologies, or familiar technologies in new data contexts - share what you learn with the organisation, explaining potential benefits, risks, and practical considerations - recommend, design and implement innovative data solutions based on organisation objectives, user needs, and operational constraints

You can: - understand and apply data governance structures and principles over a data life cycle, ensuring best practice at each phase - demonstrate knowledge of data governance industry standards - design and implement continuous improvements to optimise data governance over a data life cycle - work with internal and external stakeholders to build organisational capacity and capability in data governance

You can: - recommend data literacy as a valuable skill across all levels of the organisation - identify employee training courses and other opportunities to improve the organisation’s data literacy skills and data-driven culture

You can: - advocate for effective data governance and data management policies and guidelines within your team and across your organisation - monitor and improve data management practices in your team - help define, develop and support the use of data management tools, procedures and methods in compliance with data governance policies
You can: - lead the implementation of data best practices - communicate opportunities to improve data maturity - lead on monitoring and improving areas of data maturity

You can: - create data standards for different subjects and ensure senior leaders understand them - work with subject matter experts across the organisation to introduce data standards best practice - monitor compliance with policies and standards in the organisation - make recommendations about how the organisation should resolve breaches of standards
You can: - work with higher impact or more complex risks, advising on the impact and whether it's within risk tolerance - apply different risk methodologies in proportion to the risk

You can: - work with the team to develop and maintain an understanding of stakeholders - work with the team to develop and implement stakeholder communications strategies - identify and resolve issues, influence stakeholders and manage relationships effectively - build long-term strategic relationships and communicate clearly and regularly with stakeholders

You can: - define strategies and policies, providing guidance to others on working in the strategic context - evaluate current strategies to ensure business requirements are being met and exceeded where possible

You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload

You can: - lead data protection impact assessments and information sharing agreements - advise teams on lawful basis, consent, confidentiality, and retention - investigate incidents and recommend improvements
You can: - define data quality rules and measures - work with data providers to fix the root causes of poor quality

You can: - design data models and reference sets using clinical terminologies - map between terminologies and classifications, and explain the limits of a mapping - advise teams on terminology use in products and analytics
You can: - read and use FHIR resources, profiles, and APIs - build or test simple integrations under guidance - check messages against a specification

You can: - design pseudonymisation and linkage methods that keep identifiers separate from analysis data - assess the re-identification risk of a data set or publication and choose suitable controls - advise teams on safe settings, such as trusted research environments
You can: - run the risk process for a directorate or programme - assess risks against the risk appetite and escalate them - report on risks to committees
You can: - line manage a team, setting objectives and running appraisals - support wellbeing and manage attendance, performance, and conduct - plan the team's development and succession
You can: - track spending against a small budget and raise variances - authorise spending within your limit
